title: ICC-ES ESR-3373: ZIP System R-Sheathing (insulated sheathing with factory-bonded WRB facer)
jurisdiction: United States (ICC-ES evaluation report under IBC/IRC); NON-ALBERTA COMPARATIVE ONLY: cannot establish Alberta performance, acceptance or equivalence; no Canadian or Alberta approval is claimed or implied
code_edition: 2024, 2021 and 2018 IBC, IRC and IECC (report §1.1, p1)
document_date: Reissued June 2025; supplements revised October 2025; subject to renewal June 2027 (p1, p7)

facts.text: Report holder HUBER ENGINEERED WOODS, LLC; subject is ZIP System R-Sheathing, evaluated for structural, thermal resistance, air leakage and weather resistance.
Panels must be manufactured, identified and installed per the report and the manufacturer's installation instructions; the report governs a conflict.
When required by the code official, the report and installation instructions must be submitted at permit application.
'Fire-resistance-rated construction is outside the scope of this report.'

Special inspection for sheathing in shear walls per 2024 and 2021 IBC §§1704.3 and 1705.12 for listed exposures and wind speeds; combined wind uplift and shear use must be approved by the code official.
Panels are laminated at facilities in Camp Hill, Pennsylvania; Diboll, Texas; East Moline, Illinois; Hazle Township, Pennsylvania; and Northglenn, Colorado.

Evidence listed: AC310 (January 2024) for water-resistive membranes factory-bonded to structural sheathing used as WRBs; AC269.2 (24) (May 2025) for shear walls; an IRC intermittent-braced-wall alternative.

limitations: Non-Alberta comparative attachment; the report does not reference NBC(AE) 2023 and is not evidence of Alberta or Canadian acceptance.
